items.title: Quasi-coherence for the chaotic topology: sections of a quasi-coherent module form a base-changed module
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-modules.tex (Modules on Sites)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes quasi-coherence of a module on a category endowed with the chaotic topology by the condition that for every morphism U -> V the canonical base-change map F(V) tensor_{O(V)} O(U) -> F(U) is an isomorphism. The forward direction uses that in the chaotic topology every covering is an isomorphism, so quasi-coherence provides a presentation of the restriction of F to C/V whose sections compute F(V) because taking sections is exact; the same computation over U, together with the presentation, shows the displayed map is an isomorphism (proof lines 3554-3576). The converse reconstructs the required presentations from the module-theoretic base-change condition, completing the proof up to line 3593. H2: the translation between sheaf-theoretic quasi-coherence and the module-theoretic base-change condition is the substance.
